- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model often overshoots after a sharp upward spike in price — cap forecast at 1–2% below the peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast slope or add downward bias in second half.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 70–72 range, model tends to hold or overreact — apply mild downward correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for smoothing out overfitting.
